input.description: The file or directory to measure. A path given to jint run overrides it.

inputType.description: Whether input is a file or a directory.

include.description: The files jint reads, and the default scope of every rule.

exclude.description: The files jint skips. Exclude always wins over include.

use.description: The rules to run: names from a rule domain, or full rule objects.

name.description: The rule id: findings join back to it. Two entries with one name are a config error unless the later one sets override.

instructions.description: The yes/no question the model answers, specific to the rule's claim. Required - a generic fallback question would silently recalibrate every classification.

criteria.description: The two-sided contract: true names the exact observable condition for yes, false for no. The defect side decides the handle direction.

anyOf.description: A qualified capture address {grammar}:{capture} (e.g. markdown:section): targets the named grammar's own capture. Unknown grammar or capture is a setup error.
A qualified capture address {grammar}:{capture} (e.g. markdown:section): targets the named grammar's own capture. Unknown grammar or capture is a setup error.

Score handler (score rules only): one level per criteria entry, indexed by score 0..N. Direction is expressed by the map itself (high-bad: [pass, pass, warn, error]; high-good: [error, warn, pass, pass]). The length MUST equal the criteria count and at least one level must be non-pass. An optional per-tier message (author feedback) becomes the finding's note when the tier fires; absent = a bare finding.

message.description: The rule author's feedback; the finding's note when this tier fires.

anyOf.description: Choice handler (choice rules only): one tier per option label, keyed by the label. The option probabilities are summed per tier; the tier with the most probability is the verdict, and its most probable option's message becomes the finding's note. Options are unordered, nothing is averaged. The labels MUST equal the criteria labels and at least one tier must be non-pass. Optional undecided { margin, level, message? }: when the top tier's probability leads the runner-up tier's by less than `margin` (between 0 and 1), this tier fires instead - an undecided classification the rule acts on like any other tier.

message.description: The rule author's feedback; the finding's note when this tier fires.

anyOf.description: Noul handler (noul rules only): per-threshold comparison operators declare the direction. Declare at least one tier - warn, error, or both; a handle with neither is rejected. An error-only handle fires error past its threshold and passes otherwise. When both tiers are present, warn is the wider region and error the strictly narrower one (same direction, ordered toward the defect: greater warn < greater error, or less warn > less error). silent_band [lo, hi] keeps raw-p classifications inside it silent (must be ordered, must not cover the whole scale, must not contain any declared threshold value); absent = everything surfaces.

warn.description: One threshold comparison: exactly one operator. The operator IS the defect direction - greater_than fires on high readings, less_than on low ones. Within (0, 1).

anyOf.description: Fires when the raw value is strictly greater.

secretDenylist.description: Replaces the built-in denylist of secret-shaped files (gitignore patterns).

disable.description: Rule names to remove after the rules are composed.

concurrency.description: The most classifier calls in flight, run-wide. Default 16, max 64.

timeout.description: The time one classifier call may take, retries included, in seconds. Default 30. Each attempt gets a third of it.

maxInputTokens.description: The most input tokens the model accepts in one call. A call over it is skipped with a note. Unset: elements over 30000 tokens are skipped.

charsPerToken.description: The characters of a request's JSON that count as one token, when sizing a call against maxInputTokens. Default 4. Use a lower number for a model whose tokenizer splits code finely.
